text: DSH Bot · Model Router 是面向 DeepSeek Harness 网页端的模型路由与 Bot 工作区插件。它把任务路由器和持久 Bot 产品组合为同一入口，可从已配置的模型路线规划执行，也能选择官方 CLI 工具。用户可以比较经济、均衡和质量优先方案，拆分团队任务，并查看预算、执行记录与反馈；完整 Bot 工作区还提供多 Bot 协作和远程电脑入口。适合希望在一个 Harness 工作区规划、跟踪多模型任务的用户；模型凭据沿用 Harness 配置，CLI 按所选工具账号使用。

DSH Bot · Model Router plans tasks across configured Harness models with economy, balanced, and quality presets. It tracks budgets and run history, and the full workspace adds Bot collaboration and remote computers. Provider credentials use Harness settings.

Help me choose a configured model route based on task difficulty and budget.

DSH Bot · Model Router 的功能「路由规划」：根据任务内容、可用路线、质量与价格证据生成候选模型方案，并可采用经济、均衡或质量优先预设。
DSH Bot · Model Router 的功能「团队任务」：把复合任务规划为依赖步骤，并为各步骤分配已配置模型路线。
DSH Bot · Model Router 的功能「执行记录」：运行后可查询计划和账本中的状态、支出及结果摘要，供用户检查后续步骤。
DSH Bot · Model Router 的功能「官方 CLI 工具」：检查已登记工具并提供安装、修复、卸载及终端相关工具接口。
DSH Bot · Model Router 的功能「远程桌面」：完整工作区可选择已配对电脑，连接后观看画面或取得鼠标键盘控制权。

@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · Installation：1. Open **Plugins → Add plugin** in Harness Desktop and enter **one** package:
   - Full workspace: `@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot@0.64.0`
   - Routing only: `@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-router@0.64.0`
2. Enable it, fully quit Harness **including its tray process**, then restart so the Host loads the installed version.
3. Configure provider credentials and models in the official Harness **Models** settings. Open the Bot workspace for the full edition, or **Model Router** in the sidebar for the routing-only edition.

@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · Complete your first task：The model-routing workbench is available in both editions. In the full Bot workspace, open **Advanced workbench**.

@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · Complete your first task：1. **Prepare a model.** Add a working provider/model in Harness. In **Model configuration**, refresh routes and enter known prices and capabilities. Leave unknown information blank.
2. **Describe the result.** In **Task & execution**, choose **Project check**, **Organize documentation**, or **Compare approaches**, then edit the task and acceptance criteria. **Undo template** restores your previous text.
3. **Go to the preview.** Click **Next: preview execution**, then **Preview execution plan**. Check the selected models/tools, workspace, permissions, and estimated API cost or subscription usage.
4. **Confirm the run.** Read the confirmation items and choose **Confirm all and execute**. Creating or previewing a plan does not invoke a model; confirmation starts execution.
5. **Inspect the result.** Open **Execution history** for output, receipts, status, cancellation, and supported retry actions. Verify the requested artifact before treating the task as complete.

@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · Delegate from a Main Bot to execution Bots：1. Configure the Main Bot and execution Bots with their actual models, allowed tools, computer/workspace grants, and funding settings.
2. Open **Tasks → Bot routing**, enable it, select **Economy**, **Balanced**, or **Quality first**, and save the policy.
3. Enter a task and choose automatic routing or a specific Bot. Select the computer/directory and operation type if required. **Preview route** explains the selection, missing conditions, rejection reasons, and proposed bindings.
4. Choose **Create task with this route** to dispatch. Follow the task record and inspect the output. An accepted plan ID means submitted, not completed.

text: @ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · Delegate from a Main Bot to execution Bots：The Main Bot can also call `bot_route_task` or its alias `bot_dispatch`. Both dispatch by default; `preview: true` only previews. `bot_task_plan_status` returns the actual plan/task state. Each execution Bot's model call has its own budget admission and receipt linked to the parent task. Role text does not grant tool or computer permissions.

text: @ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · Record and replay a routine：**Full Bot edition.** Routines save a demonstrated desktop sequence privately for the selected Bot.

@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · Record and replay a routine：1. Connect to the desktop, take control, restore the application to a known starting state, enter a routine name, and choose **Start recording**.
2. Demonstrate the workflow. Only successfully acknowledged inputs are recorded; mouse movement is sampled into 200 ms waypoints.
3. Choose **Stop and save**. Saving waits for queued input and confirmed release of held keys/buttons. Recorded text is part of the saved routine.
4. Open **Routines**, select the Bot/computer, restore the same starting layout, and run the saved sequence. Check the result and any stopped step.

@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · Record and replay a routine：A routine holds up to **200 retained steps**, with pauses up to **60 seconds**, and checks display identity, physical resolution, coordinates, and recorded DPI. It replays coordinates and timing, so application/layout changes may require a new recording. If an input may have taken effect but its acknowledgement was lost, the result is **unknown**. Inspect the real desktop and provide a reconciliation note before unblocking another run. A stop request remains pending until stopping is confirmed.

Name filtering narrows the current folder. **Search text** scans the selected Bot's private text files and returns file paths, line numbers, and matching lines; open a result to edit and explicitly save the file.
section: Give each Bot a private file library

text: @ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · Give each Bot a private file library：Binary transfers preserve the original bytes, with a **16 MiB per-file limit**; text reading/editing is limited to **1 MiB per file**. Same-name uploads are rejected. Authorized `bot_library_search` calls use the calling Bot's own library. PDF/Office uploads are stored as files; searchable text here is not a general OCR or semantic-indexing service.

@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · Understand execution and accounting：- **Plan locally.** Route comparison and execution preflight do not call models. Confirmed execution sends the selected task/context to a provider or CLI and may incur charges.
- **Control API spending.** Per-task estimates and daily/monthly limits check recorded spend plus active reservations. Unknown prices or amounts require the relevant confirmation under a finite budget. Estimates are planning controls; provider bills remain authoritative.
- **Track subscriptions separately.** Subscription calls and reported input/output/cache tokens are recorded independently of API money. Missing usage remains unknown and does not imply zero usage or prove a vendor's remaining quota.
- **Choose fallback behavior.** Billing preferences can favor subscription, require subscription, or use API only. A subscription-to-API change requires fresh API estimation, budget admission, and any required confirmation. Managed editable/single-tool/team runs do not automatically retry on API.
- **Recover from evidence.** Execution records retain attempts, receipts, reservations, and unknown effects. Review interrupted work before re

@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · Integration, data, and compatibility：The Host owns committed model, tool, computer, funding, and operation identity. Bot dispatch, model-originated tools, and owner workbench actions follow this authority. Worktree isolation organizes code changes; vendor-native processes use the current user's system access.

@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · Integration, data, and compatibility：Provider credentials and authenticated sessions are managed by Harness. Routing state, receipts, committed Bot bindings, private libraries, and routine ledgers live under `<DSH_HOME>/model-router/`. The configured Bot home stores upstream conversations, memory, browser state, and team files. Agent configuration and pairing credentials remain on the controlled computer. Back up these locations before changing runtime ownership; keep pairing files, recordings, logs, and private files out of public reports.

@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · Actual cost versus planning estimate：The formula below applies to API-billed results. Algorithmic route-price comparisons are planning inputs; they do not turn a subscription into an API bill. The execution preview separates API money from estimated subscription tokens.

@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · Actual cost versus planning estimate：$`C_a`$ is `actualUsd`; $`I_u`$, $`O`$, $`R`$, and $`W`$ correspond to `inputTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cacheReadTokens`, and `cacheWriteTokens`. $`p_i`$, $`p_o`$, $`p_r`$, and $`p_w`$ are the matching input, output, cache-read and cache-write prices in USD per million tokens.

@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · Actual cost versus planning estimate：These ledger counters are disjoint after adapter normalization; do not add cached tokens to an inclusive input count. Missing optional cache prices use the input price. Incomplete usage, absent prices or unknown/unmatched identity keep the amount `null`, not zero. Complete terminal evidence can survive a failed/cancelled/timed-out run; partial events are marked `usageIncomplete`.

@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · Actual cost versus planning estimate：For example, a complete API result with 1,000 uncached input tokens at \$1/million and 500 output tokens at \$5/million costs \$0.0035. A subscription result instead records the reported tokens and call count; it is not converted to API money. A provider-reported \$0 for an API attempt is explicit evidence for that attempt, not proof that earlier unknown attempts were free. Actual provider bills are authoritative. Official-team mode does not automatically fall back to API, but a vendor CLI using its own API credentials still incurs API-billed usage.
@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · Actual cost versus planning estimate：

@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · How routing works：Manual assignment: after planning, choose algorithm recommendations or select an API model / official tool for each package. See the [workbench workflow](#workbench).

@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · How routing works：The planner is a deterministic local heuristic, not a trained success predictor. It classifies text, estimates complexity, creates suitable analysis/execution/verification/synthesis packages, discovers exact configured routes, overlays profiles, and applies capability/quality constraints. An explicit route bypasses comparison with other routes. Catalog quality/latency/risk hints are experimental priors, not measured success probabilities or live vendor quotes. Execution is currently text-oriented; a vision label does not establish an end-to-end multimodal pipeline.

@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · Token and price estimate：Without matching resource evidence, base input tokens are $`\max(80,\lceil n/3.7\rceil)`$, then adjusted by package-stage multipliers. Base output is 900, adjusted by stage/reasoning effort, with minimum 220. Here $`n`$ is the JavaScript `text.length` value. This is a text-length heuristic, not a vendor tokenizer. Sufficient matching, complete history replaces these heuristics with empirical P90 resource estimates, without applying effort or stage multipliers again. Let $`I`$ be total estimated input, $`R`$/$`W`$ the cached-read/write portions, $`O`$ output, and prices USD per million tokens:

@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · Token and price estimate：$`U_c`$ is `costUtility`. The price symbols are the same as above. $`C_{\mathrm{ref}}`$ uses fixed reference prices (input 1, output 5, cache read/write 1 USD/million), not a vendor offer. Fixed scaling prevents an unrelated expensive candidate from flattening all cost penalties. Unknown prices produce a public estimate of `null` and cost utility 0. Internal unconstrained search uses a cost sentinel of 0, but finite-budget assignment excludes unknown-price candidates; the sentinel never means free execution.

@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · Candidate objective and quality floors：With normalized quality $`q`$ and normalized latency, specialty, reasoning-fit and risk proxies:

<!-- formula:latency-utility -->
```math
L = \begin{cases}
\dfrac{1}{1+t/10\,000}, & t\text{ known}, \\
1-\min(1,\max(0,\ell e_\ell)), & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}

<!-- formula:candidate-utility -->
```math
u = w_q q+w_c U_c+w_\ell L+w_s s+w_r r-w_k k-\alpha\max(0,f-q)+\Delta_p
```

@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · Candidate objective and quality floors：<!-- formula:assignment-score -->
```math
S = \sum_{j=1}^{n}u_j - 0.015\sum_{(i,j)\in E}\mathbf{1}[\rho_i\ne\rho_j]
```

@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · Candidate objective and quality floors：$`L`$ is latency utility: $`t`$ is the matching historical P90 duration in milliseconds; otherwise $`\ell`$ is the latency proxy and $`e_\ell`$ its effort multiplier. In the utility formula, $`s`$/$`r`$/$`k`$ are specialty/reasoning-fit/risk, $`f`$ is the quality floor, $`\alpha`$ is criticality, and $`\Delta_p`$ is the bounded `preferenceAdjustment`; the $`w`$ terms are the corresponding weights. $`S`$ is `assignmentScore`; $`E`$ contains dependency edges, and $`\rho_j`$ is package $`j`$'s `provider/model` route. The indicator is 1 when routes differ, otherwise 0.

@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · Candidate objective and quality floors：Quality first uses sufficient matching objective task evidence, then falls back to task-category LiveBench, overall LiveBench, and profile/catalog estimates. Model and effort are compared jointly only when at least two API efforts have usable task evidence; observed duration can replace the latency proxy. Public-data refresh is opt-in. Human ratings affect only the bounded `preferenceAdjustment`; they cannot increase objective quality or satisfy its floor.

@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · Candidate objective and quality floors：| Package basis | Quality | Cost | Latency | Specialty | Reasoning | Risk |

Quality-first multiplies quality/cost/specialty/reasoning by 1.35/0.5/1.2/1.2 and raises the floor by 0.04. Tilted weights are renormalized to the original total; adjusted floors are clamped to [0.5, 0.97]. Balanced applies no tilt.

@ljwei-stak/dsh-model-route-bot README · Candidate pruning and assignment search：1. Prefer candidates meeting each package's floor. If none qualify, retain up to three highest-quality fallbacks and report relaxation.
2. Keep at most **12 candidates per package**, including anchors for lowest known cost, greatest utility and highest quality. Local Pareto pruning is disabled when dependencies exist, because route identity affects handoffs.
3. Validate unique package IDs and topological dependency order. Search the retained Cartesian space exactly when its size is at most **4,096**; otherwise use **beam width 256**. Search compresses dominated prefixes sharing the same future dependency boundary and ranks them using optimistic future handoffs. Remaining minimum costs prune infeasible prefixes; the beam protects the cheapest feasible prefix under a finite budget.
4. Compare assignments lexicographically: fewer relaxed packages, smaller quality shortfall, higher utility, lower cost, fewer route switches, then stable route order. Minimum-cost mode compares cost before utility. Each dependency crossing a `provider/model` route subtracts 0.015 from utility.
